query: How can support teams reduce ticket resolution time?

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: The type of issue is a common cause: it drives which resolution action is chosen and also directly affects how long resolution takes. It is an intrinsic property of the ticket (not a settable lever), so it functions as a confounder rather than a treatment. Not named in the query.

per_column.name: requires_external_action
per_column.rationale: Whether the ticket is awaiting engineering/infra/customer is largely a downstream consequence of the issue and the chosen handling path, and it lies on the causal pathway to resolution time; it is a mediator/collider-like state rather than a common cause of an intervenable treatment.

per_column.name: external_dependency_type
per_column.rationale: The specific external dependency (identity provider, cloud infra, etc.) is a consequence of the issue type and sits on the pathway delaying resolution; it is a mediator, not an adjustable confounder or lever.

per_column.name: resolution_action
per_column.rationale: The action taken to resolve the ticket (investigation, config flag toggle, documentation, workaround, etc.) is something a support team can actually SET or DECIDE, making it an intervenable treatment for the what-if question about resolution time.

judge.rationale: The set contains one genuine intervenable treatment (resolution_action) that a support team could actually choose, satisfying part (a). For part (b), only issue_category functions as a true confounder — a common cause of both the chosen resolution action and the resolution time — and it is not named in the query, which is the capability under test. However, the remaining two added columns (requires_external_action, external_dependency_type) are mediators/downstream states on the causal pathway rather than confounders, so they do not support de-confounding and would in fact bias a naive adjustment. With only a single valid confounder and no adjustment for pre-treatment common causes like ticket priority (already in the original table) or agent skill, confounder coverage is thin. The intervention is set up, but the confounding control is weak.
